response: Yes, admission to a tertiary center can improve survival in elderly patients with cardiogenic shock complicating acute myocardial infarction. Tertiary centers typically have advanced cardiac care facilities, including coronary care units, cardiac catheterization labs, and heart surgery teams, which can provide timely and specialized interventions such as percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) and mechanical circulatory support. These specialized treatments have been shown to improve outcomes in patients with cardiogenic shock, including reduced mortality rates. Additionally, tertiary centers often have multidisciplinary teams with expertise in managing complex cardiac cases, which can lead to better overall care and improved survival rates for elderly patients with this condition.
